Microscopic observation of mitosis in onion roots depends heavily on the quality of the stain and the squash technique; failure to see clear phases is common and should be supplemented with prepared slides or digital micrographs.
Embryogenesis is highly simplified to the blastula and gastrula stages, omitting complex organogenesis to fit the primary education abstraction level.

The distinction between sexual and asexual reproduction in plants (e.g., spores vs. seeds) is simplified; the alternation of generations in mosses and ferns may require careful teacher guidance to avoid confusing haploid/diploid life stages.
scoring_rule: Pass if the student clearly distinguishes the hollow structure of the blastula from the layered/folded structure of the gastrula.
